leftEvidence.title: Royal justice, abundance, and a closing David notice

points.label: Action and response
points.left: The prayer asks judgment for the king, defense of the poor, wide dominion, tribute, rescue, abundance, enduring name, and blessing; it closes by saying David’s prayers are ended.
points.right: The song rejoices in going to the LORD’s house, sees Jerusalem built compactly, names tribal ascent and David’s thrones, and prays for peace.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places a royal vision ends with an editorial statement about David’s prayers inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places David’s house is located within pilgrimage, judgment, and Jerusalem’s peace inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Psalms 72:1–20 and Psalms 122:1–9 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Royal, Poetic, and Prophetic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: Psalms 72:1–20 foregrounds a royal vision ends with an editorial statement about David’s prayers; Psalms 122:1–9 foregrounds David’s house is located within pilgrimage, judgment, and Jerusalem’s peace. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
